Astronaut [John Young](/wiki/John_Young_(astronaut) "John Young (astronaut)") jumping on the Moon, illustrating that the [gravitational pull](/wiki/Gravitational_acceleration "Gravitational acceleration") of the Moon is approximately 1/6 of Earth's. The jumping height is limited by the EVA space suit's weight on the Moon of about 13.6 kg (30 lb) and by the suit's pressurization resisting the bending of the suit, as needed for jumping.[[85]](#cite_note-Kluger_2018_z081-93)[[86]](#cite_note-Nast_2013_v237-94)

On average the Moon's [surface gravity](/wiki/Surface_gravity "Surface gravity") is 1.62 [m/s2](/wiki/Metre_per_second_squared "Metre per second squared")[[5]](#cite_note-NSSDC-7) (0.1654 [g](/wiki/G-force "G-force"); 5.318 [ft/s2](/wiki/Foot_per_second_squared "Foot per second squared")), about half of the surface gravity of [Mars](/wiki/Mars "Mars") and about a sixth of Earth's.

The [Moon's gravitational field](/wiki/Gravitation_of_the_Moon "Gravitation of the Moon") is not uniform. The details of the gravitational field have been measured through tracking the [Doppler shift](/wiki/Doppler_shift "Doppler shift") of radio signals emitted by [orbiting spacecraft](/wiki/Lunar_orbiter "Lunar orbiter"). The main lunar gravity features are [mascons](/wiki/Mass_concentration_(astronomy) "Mass concentration (astronomy)"), large positive gravitational anomalies associated with some of the giant impact basins, partly caused by the dense mare basaltic lava flows that fill those basins.[[87]](#cite_note-95)[[88]](#cite_note-96) The anomalies greatly influence the [orbit of spacecraft about the Moon](/wiki/Lunar_orbit "Lunar orbit"). After her service in the [White House](/wiki/White_House "White House") and her lapsed judicial nomination, Kagan returned to academia in 1999. She initially sought to return to the University of Chicago, but she had given up her tenured position during her extended stint in the Clinton Administration, and the school chose not to rehire her, reportedly due to doubts about her commitment to academia.[[54]](#cite_note-56) Kagan quickly found a position as a visiting professor at Harvard Law School. While there, she authored a law review article on [United States administrative law](/wiki/United_States_administrative_law "United States administrative law"), focusing on the president's role in formulating and influencing federal administrative law. The article was honored as the year's top scholarly article by the [American Bar Association](/wiki/American_Bar_Association "American Bar Association")'s Section on Administrative Law and Regulatory Practice.[[55]](#cite_note-57)

In 2001, Kagan was named a full professor at Harvard Law School and in 2003 she was named dean of the Law School by Harvard University President [Lawrence Summers](/wiki/Lawrence_Summers "Lawrence Summers").[[56]](#cite_note-Berman2008-58) She succeeded [Robert C. Since 1635, the [Académie Française](/wiki/Acad%C3%A9mie_Fran%C3%A7aise "Académie Française") has been the official authority on the French language, although its recommendations carry no legal weight. There are also regional languages spoken in France, such as [Occitan](/wiki/Occitan_language "Occitan language"), [Breton](/wiki/Breton_language "Breton language"), [Catalan](/wiki/Catalan_language "Catalan language"), [Flemish](/wiki/French_Flemish "French Flemish") ([Dutch](/wiki/Dutch_language "Dutch language") dialect), [Alsatian](/wiki/Alsatian_dialect "Alsatian dialect") (German dialect), [Basque](/wiki/Basque_language "Basque language"), and [Corsican](/wiki/Corsican_language "Corsican language") (Italian dialect). Italian was the official language of Corsica up to 1859.[[272]](#cite_note-283) Although regional languages do not have the status of official languages, they are recognised by Article 75-1 of the constitution as part of France's heritage.[[273]](#cite_note-284)

Colorectal cancer :: Prevention :: Lifestyle :: chunk_0014
Lifestyle risk factors with strong evidence include lack of exercise, cigarette smoking, alcohol, and obesity.[[105]](#cite_note-NCI2018Overview-105)[[106]](#cite_note-WHOcancerprevention-106)[[107]](#cite_note-107) The risk of colon cancer can be reduced by maintaining a normal body weight through a combination of sufficient exercise and eating a [healthy diet](/wiki/Healthy_diet "Healthy diet").[[108]](#cite_note-108)

Current research consistently links eating more red meat and processed meat to a higher risk of the disease.[[109]](#cite_note-109) Starting in the 1970s, dietary recommendations to prevent colorectal cancer often included increasing the consumption of [whole grains](/wiki/Whole_grain "Whole grain"), fruits and vegetables, and reducing the intake of [red meat](/wiki/Red_meat "Red meat") and [processed meats](/wiki/Processed_meat "Processed meat"). This was based on animal studies and retrospective observational studies. However, large-scale prospective studies have failed to demonstrate a significant protective effect, and due to the multiple causes of cancer and the complexity of studying correlations between diet and health, it is uncertain whether any specific dietary interventions will have significant protective effects.[[110]](#cite_note-WCR2014Willett-110): 432–433[[111]](#cite_note-WCR2014_2.6-111): 125–126 In 2018 the [National Cancer Institute](/wiki/National_Cancer_Institute "National Cancer Institute") stated that "There is no reliable evidence that a diet started in adulthood that is low in fat and meat and high in fiber, fruits, and vegetables reduces the risk of CRC by a clinically important degree."[[105]](#cite_note-NCI2018Overview-105)[[112]](#cite_note-NCI2018Evidence-112)

Consuming alcoholic drinks and consuming processed meat both increase the risk of colorectal cancer.[[113]](#cite_note-w151-113)

YouTube began as a [venture capital](/wiki/Venture_capital "Venture capital")–funded technology [startup](/wiki/Startup_company "Startup company"). Between November 2005 and April 2006, the company raised money from various investors, with [Sequoia Capital](/wiki/Sequoia_Capital "Sequoia Capital") and Artis Capital Management being the largest two.[[15]](#cite_note-Jackpot-15)[[23]](#cite_note-23) YouTube's early headquarters were situated above a pizzeria and a Japanese restaurant in [San Mateo](/wiki/San_Mateo,_California "San Mateo, California"), California.[[24]](#cite_note-24) In February 2005, the company registered `www.youtube.com`.[[25]](#cite_note-25) The first video was uploaded on April 23, 2005. Titled "[Me at the zoo](/wiki/Me_at_the_zoo "Me at the zoo")", it shows co-founder Jawed Karim at the [San Diego Zoo](/wiki/San_Diego_Zoo "San Diego Zoo") and can still be viewed on the site.[[26]](#cite_note-26)[[27]](#cite_note-27) The same day, the company launched a public [beta](/wiki/Software_release_life_cycle "Software release life cycle") and by November, a [Nike](/wiki/Nike,_Inc. "Nike, Inc.") ad featuring [Ronaldinho](/wiki/Ronaldinho "Ronaldinho") became the first video to reach one million total views.[[28]](#cite_note-28)[[29]](#cite_note-29) The site exited beta in December 2005, by which time the site was receiving 8 million views a day.[[30]](#cite_note-30)[[31]](#cite_note-31) Clips at the time were limited to 100 megabytes, as little as 30 seconds of footage.[[32]](#cite_note-32)

YouTube was not the first video-sharing site on the Internet; [Vimeo](/wiki/Vimeo "Vimeo") was founded in November 2004, though that site remained a side project of its developers from [CollegeHumor](/wiki/CollegeHumor "CollegeHumor").[[33]](#cite_note-fortune_vimeo-33) On December 17, 2005, the same week YouTube exited beta, NBCUniversal *[Saturday Night Live](/wiki/Saturday_Night

Main article: [British Hong Kong](/wiki/British_Hong_Kong "British Hong Kong")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3f/Hong_Kong_1868.jpg/250px-Hong_Kong_1868.jpg)](/wiki/File:Hong_Kong_1868.jpg)

Hong Kong in 1868, photograph by [John Thomson](/wiki/John_Thomson_(photographer) "John Thomson (photographer)")

In 1839, the [Daoguang Emperor](/wiki/Daoguang_Emperor "Daoguang Emperor") rejected proposals to legalise and tax [opium](/wiki/Opium "Opium") and ordered imperial commissioner [Lin Zexu](/wiki/Lin_Zexu "Lin Zexu") to eradicate the opium trade. The commissioner destroyed opium stockpiles and halted all foreign trade,[[48]](#cite_note-54) triggering a British military response and the [First Opium War](/wiki/First_Opium_War "First Opium War"). The Qing surrendered early in the war and ceded Hong Kong Island in the [Convention of Chuenpi](/wiki/Convention_of_Chuenpi "Convention of Chuenpi"), signed by [Charles Elliot](/wiki/Charles_Elliot "Charles Elliot") and [Qishan](/wiki/Qishan_(official) "Qishan (official)"). British forces began controlling Hong Kong shortly after the signing of the convention, on 26 January 1841.[[49]](#cite_note-55) However, both countries were dissatisfied and did not ratify the agreement.[[50]](#cite_note-56) After more than a year of further hostilities, Hong Kong Island was formally ceded to the [United Kingdom](/wiki/United_Kingdom_of_Great_Britain_and_Ireland "United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland") in the 1842 [Treaty of Nanking](/wiki/Treaty_of_Nanking "Treaty of Nanking").[[51]](#cite_note-Courtauld-57)

Administrative infrastructure was quickly built by early 1842, but piracy, disease, and hostile Qing policies initially prevented the government from attracting commerce. > "I have seen the player who will inherit my place in Argentinian football and his name is Messi."

— [Diego Maradona](/wiki/Diego_Maradona "Diego Maradona") hailing the 18-year-old Messi as his successor in February 2006[[296]](#cite_note-successor-319)

Throughout his career, Messi has been compared with [Diego Maradona](/wiki/Diego_Maradona "Diego Maradona"), who was also considered the best player of his generation and one of the greatest in the history of the sport.[[297]](#cite_note-adept-320)[[298]](#cite_note-321) The comparisons stem broadly from both players' short statures, their similar playing styles as left-footed [playmakers](/wiki/Playmaker "Playmaker"), and their shared nationality as Argentines.[[299]](#cite_note-Daily-322) Initially, Messi was merely one of many young Argentine players to receive the "New Maradona" moniker, but as his career progressed, he proved his similarity beyond all previous contenders, establishing himself as the best player Argentina had produced since Maradona.[[40]](#cite_note-Aimar-46)[[300]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTELisi2011533–539-323) When Messi was 18 years old, Maradona called him the best player in the world and hailed him as his successor.[[296]](#cite_note-successor-319) From 2008 through the [2010 FIFA World Cup](/wiki/2010_FIFA_World_Cup "2010 FIFA World Cup"), Messi played for Argentina's [national team](/wiki/Argentina_national_football_team "Argentina national football team") while Maradona managed the team, and it was during this period that Messi was given the number 10 shirt that Maradona famously wore. Maradona gave Messi his blessing, telling him: "the No 10 is yours. There's nobody better than you to wear it."[[206]](#cite_note-telegraph.co.uk-220)

Main article: [Bronx High School of Science](/wiki/Bronx_High_School_of_Science "Bronx High School of Science")

Bronx High School of Science was founded in 1938 as a specialized science and math high school for boys, by resolution of the [Board of Education of the City of New York](/wiki/Board_of_Education_of_the_City_of_New_York "Board of Education of the City of New York"), with [Morris Meister](/wiki/Morris_Meister "Morris Meister") as the first principal of the school. They were given use of an antiquated Gothic-gargoyled edifice located at Creston Avenue and 184th Street. The building, built in 1918 for Evander Childs High School, had been successively occupied by [Walton High School](/wiki/Walton_High_School_(New_York_City) "Walton High School (New York City)") (1930) and by an annex of [DeWitt Clinton High School](/wiki/DeWitt_Clinton_High_School "DeWitt Clinton High School") (1935). The initial faculty was comprised in part by a contingent from [Stuyvesant High School](/wiki/Stuyvesant_High_School "Stuyvesant High School").[[2]](#cite_note-StuyLandmark-2) Principal Meister put his imprint on the school from its formation, for example, selecting as school colors "green to represent chlorophyll and gold the sun, both of which are essential to the chain of life."[[3]](#cite_note-3)

Before the Rams’ [1979 Super Bowl season](/wiki/1979_Los_Angeles_Rams_season "1979 Los Angeles Rams season"), the team's owner [Carroll Rosenbloom](/wiki/Carroll_Rosenbloom "Carroll Rosenbloom") drowned in an accident.[[5]](#cite_note-5) His widow, [Georgia Frontiere](/wiki/Georgia_Frontiere "Georgia Frontiere"), inherited 70% ownership of the team. Frontiere fired her stepson, [Steve Rosenbloom](/wiki/Steve_Rosenbloom "Steve Rosenbloom"), and assumed total control of the franchise. As had been planned before Carroll Rosenbloom's death, the Rams moved from their longtime home at the [Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum](/wiki/Los_Angeles_Memorial_Coliseum "Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum") to [Anaheim Stadium](/wiki/Anaheim_Stadium "Anaheim Stadium") in nearby [Orange County](/wiki/Orange_County,_California "Orange County, California") in 1980. The move was necessitated in part because the Coliseum's abnormally large [seating capacity](/wiki/Seating_capacity "Seating capacity") of 100,000 was difficult to sell out,[[6]](#cite_note-6) which often subjected the team to the league's local-market TV [blackout rule](/wiki/NFL_blackout "NFL blackout"). At the same time, Southern California's population patterns were changing; there was rapid growth in L.A.’s affluent suburbs (e.g. greater Orange County) and a decline in the city of Los Angeles's population and income.[[7]](#cite_note-shopping-7) Anaheim Stadium was originally built in 1966 as the home of the [California Angels](/wiki/History_of_the_Los_Angeles_Angels "History of the Los Angeles Angels") Major League Baseball franchise. To accommodate the Rams’ move, the ballpark was reconfigured with luxury suites and enclosed to accommodate crowds of about 65,000 for football.

As of 2016, 400 million people spoke English as their [first language](/wiki/First_language "First language"), and 1.1 billion spoke it as a second language.[[70]](#cite_note-70) English is the [largest language by number of speakers](/wiki/List_of_languages_by_total_number_of_speakers "List of languages by total number of speakers"), spoken by communities on every continent.[[71]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTECrystal2003b106-71) Estimates
